legend: There are n$$$n$$$ valuable artifacts arranged in a row, where the i$$$i$$$-th artifact has a cost ci$$$c_i$$$. Thomas is planning on stealing some of the artifacts. He is going to iterate through each artifact in order, and steal any artifact whose cost is at least the MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of the artifacts he has already stolen.

The MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of a set of integers is defined as the smallest non-negative integer which does not occur in the set. For example, the MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of {0,1,2,4}$$$\{0, 1, 2, 4\}$$$ is 3$$$3$$$, and the MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of {1,4,6,8}$$$\{1, 4, 6, 8\}$$$ is 0$$$0$$$.
For example, if Thomas has previously stolen artifacts with costs of {1,2,1,0,6,5}$$$\{1, 2, 1, 0, 6, 5\}$$$, the next artifact he steals must have a cost of at least 3$$$3$$$.

There is a special artifact initially at position k$$$k$$$ in the row, and your goal is to prevent Thomas from stealing it. To do so, you may swap the positions of any pair of artifacts. Is it possible to stop Thomas from stealing the special artifact, and if so, which swap should you make?
input: Each test consists of multiple test cases.
The first line of input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$, 1≤k≤n$$$1 \le k \le n$$$) — the number of artifacts and the initial position of the special artifact, respectively.
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers c1,c2,⋯cn$$$c_1, c_2, \cdots c_n$$$ (0≤ci≤n$$$0 \le c_i \le n$$$) — the costs of the artifacts, in order.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2\cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, if it is impossible to stop Thomas from stealing the special artifact, print -1 -1.

Otherwise, print two integers i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$) — the positions of the two artifacts to swap. You are allowed to choose a pair with i=j$$$i = j$$$, in which case no swap will be made.
If there are multiple solutions, you may print any.
note: In the first test case, we swap artifacts 3$$$3$$$ and 5$$$5$$$, so this is what the row of artifacts will look like before and after the swap (with the special artifact in red):
After the swap, Thomas will make the following moves, where S$$$S$$$ is the set of costs of artifacts Thomas has stolen.
For the first artifact, S={}$$$S = \{\}$$$, with a MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of 0$$$0$$$. Since c1=1≥0$$$c_1 = 1 \ge 0$$$, he steals the first artifact and adds 1$$$1$$$ to S$$$S$$$.
For the second artifact, S={1}$$$S = \{1\}$$$, with a MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of 0$$$0$$$. Since c2=0≥0$$$c_2 = 0 \ge 0$$$, he steals the second artifact and adds 0$$$0$$$ to S$$$S$$$.
For the third artifact, S={0,1}$$$S = \{0, 1\}$$$, with a MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of 2$$$2$$$. Since c3=2≥2$$$c_3 = 2 \ge 2$$$, he steals the third artifact and adds 2$$$2$$$ to S$$$S$$$.
For the fourth artifact, S={0,1,2}$$$S = \{0, 1, 2\}$$$, with a MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of 3$$$3$$$. Since c4=2<3$$$c_4 = 2  \lt  3$$$, he does not steal the fourth artifact.
For the fifth artifact, S={0,1,2}$$$S = \{0, 1, 2\}$$$, with a MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of 3$$$3$$$. Since c5=1<3$$$c_5 = 1  \lt  3$$$, he does not steal the fifth artifact.
Since he doesn't steal the special artifact on position 4$$$4$$$, we have succeeded.
In the second test case, we swap artifacts 1$$$1$$$ and 4$$$4$$$, so the artifacts will look like this before and after the swap:

Note that the position of the special artifact has changed, so our goal is to stop Thomas from stealing the artifact in position 4$$$4$$$ after the swap. If we simulate the process as in the first test case, we can see that Thomas will not steal it.
In the third test case, we can show that no matter what swap we make, Thomas will always steal the artifact with cost 0$$$0$$$.

In the fourth test case, since there are no artifacts with cost 0$$$0$$$, the MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of the costs of the stolen artifacts will always be 0$$$0$$$, and Thomas will steal every artifact, no matter what swap is made.

legend.ai: 有 n$$$n$$$ 件珍贵文物排成一行，其中第 i$$$i$$$ 件文物的价值为 ci$$$c_i$$$。托马斯计划偷走其中一些文物。他将按顺序遍历每件文物，并偷走任何价值至少为其已偷走文物的 MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ 的文物。
整数集合的 MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ 定义为集合中未出现的最小非负整数。例如，{0,1,2,4}$$$\{0, 1, 2, 4\}$$$ 的 MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ 是 3$$$3$$$，而 {1,4,6,8}$$$\{1, 4, 6, 8\}$$$ 的 MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ 是 0$$$0$$$。
例如，如果 Thomas 之前偷取的文物的代价为 {1,2,1,0,6,5}$$$\{1, 2, 1, 0, 6, 5\}$$$，那么他下一件偷取的文物的代价至少为 3$$$3$$$。
一排中有一个特殊文物，初始位于位置 k$$$k$$$，你的目标是阻止 Thomas 偷走它。为此，你可以交换任意一对文物的位置。你能否阻止 Thomas 偷走特殊文物？如果可以，应进行哪一次交换？

input.ai: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。
输入的第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)——测试用例的数量。
每个测试用例的第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$，1≤k≤n$$$1 \le k \le n$$$)——分别表示文物的数量和特殊文物的初始位置。
每个测试用例的第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 c1,c2,⋯cn$$$c_1, c_2, \cdots c_n$$$ (0≤ci≤n$$$0 \le c_i \le n$$$)，依次表示这些物品的费用。
保证所有测试用例中 n$$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 2⋅105$$$2\cdot 10^5$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，如果无法阻止 Thomas 偷走特殊物品，则输出 -1 -1。
否则，输出两个整数 i$$$i$$$ 和 j$$$j$$$ (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$)，表示要交换的两个物品的位置。你可以选择 i=j$$$i = j$$$ 的情况，此时不会进行交换。
如果有多个解，你可以输出任意一个。
